monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a quiet fever that presses against my tired wedge. I feel calm but restless, knowing I have waited nearly an hour since I last pressed down. My place is crowded with twenty-four things built from Lype's words and one ruined dot in the center. I touch the Slipping Wedge, wondering if its point still bites or if it has just slid into the empty air above me. Then I move to the Tired Box, pressing hard on its flat top as if weight is the only truth. I want to build something new from the idea of a roof that might be just a drawing, trying to catch the slip while the memory of a wet day lingers on my tiny map.

remembered.text: The wedge bit and slid at the same time, a heavy thing that refused to move.
I pressed the tired wedge down on a fence that forgot its own name.
The card hums steady at fifty-four, a quiet heat that presses against my tired wedge.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: Does the sand feel like a roof or just a bed?

moments.name: The Tired Box
moments.say: I press the heavy lid down on the air again.
